name: Slovakian Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Sign language; only classification/lexicostatistic refs (Bickford 2005; Rutkowski & Sak 2016); no prosody/stress description located

sources.citation: Vojtechovský, Roman. 2025. Fonologické procesy v prúde posunkovania [Phonological processes in the stream of signing]. Jazykovedný časopis 76(2): 509–533. DOI 10.2478/jazcas-2025-0041 (CC BY-NC-ND).
sources.note: Whole article is SPJ phonology: five parameters (61 handshapes, 21 places, 26 movements per Posunky.sk), syllable = movement (after Sandler), and phonological processes (assimilation, reduction, elision, metathesis, epenthesis, coarticulation). Zero mention of stress, accent, prosody or rhythm (a full-text search for stress/accent prízvuk/dôraz/akcent/prozód: no hits).

sources.citation: Vojtechovský, R. – Majerčáková, D. – Hefty, M. – Vojtechovská, V. – Cehlárik, J. – Hefty, A. 2024. Slovenský posunkový jazyk pre študentov – úplných začiatočníkov I.: Ja a moja rodina. Učebný text. Trnava: Pedagogická fakulta Trnavskej univerzity. 246 pp. ISBN 978-80-568-0631-9.
sources.note: Ch. 5.1 (p. 207): lists melody, tempo, pause, prízvuk (syllable stress), dôraz (word emphasis), intensity, emphasis as spoken-language intonation and states that in sign language non-manual means express intonation, distinguishing declarative/interrogative/imperative sentences; 5.4 (p. 211) says intonation (melody, pause) matters in signed discourse. No word-level stress statement.

sources.citation: Hladký, J. – Vojtechovský, R. – Herčíková, K. – Zasina, A. J. 2025. A university study of sign language interpreting in Slovakia and Czechia. Humanities and Social Sciences Communications 12: 1122. DOI 10.1057/s41599-025-05435-1.
sources.note: Interpreter-training survey; no linguistic description of SPJ.

sources.citation: Vojtechovský, Roman. 2025. Sociolingvistická variabilita v slovenskom posunkovom jazyku. Disputationes Scientificae Universitatis Catholicae in Ružomberok 25(3): 79–101. DOI 10.54937/dspt.2025.25.3.79-101.
sources.note: Lexical/regional variation; mentions 'phonological variants' only. Nothing on stress. Its reference list is the fullest SPJ bibliography seen (Csonka–Mistrík–Ubár 1986; Tarcsiová 2012; Vojtechovský 2011, 2012, 2022; Šmehilová 2005).

sources.citation: Tarcsiová, Darina. 2024. Nepočujúci, posunkový jazyk a kultúra Nepočujúcich ako neoddeliteľná súčasť kultúry majority v európskom priestore. Slavica Slovaca 59(3): 596–603. DOI 10.31577/slavslov.2024.3.19.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic/legal overview; nothing on structure or stress.

sources.citation: Vojtechovský, Roman (ed.). 2024. Tlmočenie nielen pre nepočujúce osoby: elektronický zborník odborných príspevkov. Trnava – Bratislava: PdF TU – Snepeda. ISBN 978-80-568-0613-5.
sources.note: Interpreting proceedings; 'prozódia' appears only for spoken-Slovak interpreting quality; no SPJ stress statement.

sources.citation: Hefty, Michal – Hefty, Angela. 2022. Divadelné tlmočenie do slovenského posunkového jazyka. Trnava: Pedagogická fakulta Trnavskej univerzity.
sources.note: Theatre interpreting; rhythm discussed only for song interpretation. Nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: Vojtechovský, Roman. 2022. Klasifikátory a špecifikátory v slovenskom posunkovom jazyku. Trnava: Pedagogická fakulta Trnavskej univerzity. 119 pp.
sources.note: Classifier morphology; p. 9 defines the sign and simultaneity, mentions intonation only as a spoken-language device. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Vojtechovský, R. – Vojtechovská, V. – Poláčková, V. – Lipovská, B. 2021. Posunky.sk: Prekladový slovník slovenského jazyka – slovenského posunkového jazyka I. Trnava – Bratislava: PdF TU – Snepeda. 116 pp. ISBN 978-80-568-0446-9.
sources.note: Introduction (pp. 6–9) describes the sign as manual component (handshape, position, movement, orientation, all simultaneous) plus non-manual component (mimics, head/trunk, mouth: spoken and oral components) carrying mainly grammatical meaning (question vs statement, intensification); 'fonetické varianty' defined as one-parameter differences. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Bickford, J. Albert. 2005. The Signed Languages of Eastern Europe. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2005-026. Dallas: SIL International. 37 pp.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey and wordlist lexicostatistics; §3.12 Slovakia (p. 15) gives schools, law 149/1995, one dictionary (Csonka, Mistrík & Ubár 1986). No phonology; no stress. (downloaded via the Internet Archive; live sil.org URL is could not be reached by automated download.)
